dialog.body: Utilities billing, this is Priya. How can I help you?
Hi, yeah, good afternoon. My name's Maria Moniz. I'm calling for my mother, she's in her seventies and she rents at 187 Ocean Avenue, out on the Ocean Drive side.
Okay. And what's the question about the account?

So the landlord's telling her she owes the water and sewer bill. She's the tenant. Her lease doesn't say anything clear to me, so I just want to know whose bill it actually is. Like, who's responsible, the owner or her?
Generally the water and sewer account is billed to the property owner, and what happens between the owner and the tenant is set by the lease. Is the account in your mother's name, or the landlord's?
That I don't know. The bill comes to the house. I've seen it, it's got a name on top but I don't have it in front of me, I'm at my desk at work. Can you look it up by the address?

I can. One moment. [pause] Okay, I have the account for 187 Ocean Avenue. I can tell you it's under an owner name, not your mother's. I can't go through more detail than that with you yet, since you're not on the account.
Okay, that's fair. So it's the landlord's account. Then he's the one the city bills, and if he wants her to pay, that's between them.
That's right. The city's bill goes to the owner. Whether the tenant reimburses is a lease matter. If you have a copy of the lease, that's the place to look.
Got it. Okay. Second thing. I help her with all her bills, she's not great with the computer stuff. Can I be authorized to talk to you guys for her? So I'm not calling and getting the runaround?

We'd need the account holder to authorize that, since the account is the owner's. But if your mother is going to be responsible for payments, she can fill out an authorization form and the owner would likely need to sign off too. I can email you the form, or mail it.
Mail it to her, please. Same address, 187 Ocean. Does it need a notary? Because I'd need to get a notary stamp at the bank, and I'm only able to get there on Saturday morning.
Yes, the form asks for a notarized signature, so you'd want to sign it in front of the notary, not before. Bring ID with you.

Okay, good to know, thanks. And one more. If the bill does end up needing to get paid, can it be paid online tonight? Like after City Hall's closed? I'm not off work until late and then I've got her dinner to do.

There's an online payment option that's available any time, so tonight is fine. You'd need the account number from the bill. There's also a drop box at City Hall for checks if you'd rather do that on your way by.
Okay, the online one's better. I'll get the account number off the paper bill when I get to her place. Wicked busy week, with this rain and everything.
Understood. Is there anything else I can help with today?
No, I think that's it. So the form gets mailed to my mother at 187 Ocean, I get it notarized at the bank Saturday, and then I send it back?
Correct. Return it to our office once it's signed and notarized, and we'll process it. It'll go out in today's mail.
Perfect. Thank you, Priya.
You're welcome. Take care.
